key_insight: Risk-seeking optimization steers bosonic state preparation toward a subset of high-fidelity outcomes, trading lower average fidelity for much better best-case performance.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum engineers a tunable way to target reliable high-quality state samples when success probability matters more than average ensemble fidelity.
method: Adapt state-preparation training with risk-sensitive objectives instead of only expected fidelity.
Optimize for favorable fidelity quantiles/subsets within the stochastic photon-loss ensemble.
Adjust the objective to control the trade-off between high-fidelity probability and worst-case infidelity reached.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that some pure states in the prepared ensemble achieved infidelity reductions of up to four orders of magnitude versus standard average-fidelity optimization.
watch_item: The approach may reduce overall average fidelity, so it must be tuned carefully for applications that depend on ensemble-wide performance rather than rare high-fidelity samples.
paper_title: Steering the Fidelity in State Preparation on Noisy Bosonic Systems with Risk-Seeking Optimization
